builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Agentic Data Sampling Framework for Multilingual ASR via Linguistic-Aware Error-Driven Optimization
summary: Replaces manual, heuristic-based multilingual data sampling strategies with an LLM-agent-driven approach that selects domain-, sample-, and token-level data based on linguistic analysis of ASR errors (phonological, morphological, syntactic). Costs include the complexity of integrating an external LLM agent into the training loop, potential latency from agent-based analysis, and the engineering overhead of implementing the rubric-driven feedback system. Can fail if the linguistic rubric does not generalize across languages, if the LLM agent's sampling decisions introduce selection bias, or if the framework overfits to specific error patterns in the target languages.
rationale: This method offers a principled way to reduce data requirements and improve convergence for multilingual ASR fine-tuning, which aligns with the reader's constrained infrastructure, but its effectiveness is demonstrated only on Whisper-medium and twelve languages, so workload-specific validation is required before production adoption.
technique: Agentic linguistic-aware data sampling for multilingual ASR fine-tuning

claims.statement: Replaces manual, heuristic-based multilingual data sampling strategies with an LLM-agent-driven approach that selects domain-, sample-, and token-level data based on linguistic analysis of ASR errors (phonological, morphological, syntactic). Costs include the complexity of integrating an external LLM agent into the training loop, potential latency from agent-based analysis, and the engineering overhead of implementing the rubric-driven feedback system. Can fail if the linguistic rubric does not generalize across languages, if the LLM agent's sampling decisions introduce selection bias, or if the framework overfits to specific error patterns in the target languages.

The paper claims the agentic sampling framework achieves better performance than full-data training while using less training data and lower computational resources, and substantially accelerates training convergence compared to conventional sampling strategies, on twelve Common Voice languages using Whisper-medium as the backbone.
